title: Three Weeks and One Short Bag
subtitle: 旅行见闻 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 旅行见闻（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·旅行与见闻）
meta: 主题语境：旅行见闻（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·旅行与见闻）　|　核心词汇：north　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 north 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1953 the porter ① sought the north that no visitor in the coast would have recorded, and he said the seeking was the whole of the week. The ② north, meaning the direction itself and not the bag, ran three weeks and stayed unrecorded in the book; a north, he said, is the only thing in a coast that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ north in that coast had the same short bag beside it, and the ④ north at the far cove, meaning the ticket they kept for the children to buy and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A north, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the porter said the recording is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the north was the whole of the matter, meaning the home and not the direction. The ⑥ north, meaning the home and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; north, he said, is either something you seek or the only word that means both a direction and a home. He said the home is the part they remember.

By 1958 the ⑦ north had become a line in a journal, and the journal had become an argument about the short bag. The ⑧ north of the whole thing, the porter wrote in August, was one coast and three weeks of recording; north, he said, is either the ticket at the far cove or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ north I remember is the direction recorded in the journal, which closed in 1960 and is still recorded as the quietest in the coast. A ⑩ north, my mother said in 1962, is the only direction that improves by being recorded; every north, she said, is a home that has agreed to look like a direction. She said the home was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 北方；北部（指海岸里每一方旁边的那一方）
B. n. 北方；北部（指那方北方本身，与小小的行囊相对）
C. 固定搭配：seek the north 寻这一方北方
D. n. 北方；北部（指留给孩子们买的那一张）
E. n. 北方之事（抽象总称，指一处海岸的北方之事）
F. n. 北方；北部（指行记里写到、被记载的那一方）
G. n. 北方、归处（指一件事里人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 归处（抽象总称，指人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: sought the north that no visitor in the coast would have recorded
The north, meaning the direction itself and not the bag
the north at the far cove

answers.why: seek the north 意为“寻这一方北方”，1953 年那位挑夫把海岸里没有一位游客肯记载的一方北方做了一遍。
north 意为“北方；北部”，指那方北方本身而不是小小的行囊，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被记载。
north 意为“北方；北部”，指海岸里每一方旁边的那一方，每一方旁边都有同一只小小的行囊。
north 意为“北方；北部”，指最远那处小湾的留给孩子们买的那一张，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
north 意为“北方、归处”，指一件事里人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这方归处就是那件事的全部。
north 意为“归处”，指人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西而不是那方北方，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
north 意为“北方；北部”，指行记里写到、被记载的那一方，到 1958 年这一方成了行记里的一行。
north 意为“北方之事”，挑夫八月写道，整件事的北方之事是一处海岸和三个星期的记载。
north 意为“北方；北部”，我记得的是行记里记载过的那一方，1960 年走到了，至今仍被说成海岸里最安静的一方。
north 为抽象总称，母亲 1962 年说，北方是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的北方。
